text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Austrian Airlines has taken over 36 percent of Lauda Air and has thereby become the major shareholder of the airline. Lufthansa has reduced its stake in Lauda Air to 20 percent and offers cooperation.
- Austria's opposition parties remain sceptical of the government's reforms of immigration laws, which are to be presented today.
- Austria's postal company and postal savings bank PSK have agreed on future cooperation and a yearly 1.2 billion schilling compensation by PSK for using post offices.
- The Finance Ministry plans to introduce a reformed minimum corporate tax of five percent this month. The previous minimum corporate tax was abolished by the constitutional court.

- Secretary of State for the Finance Ministry Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer expects the introduction of Europe's single currency euro to help boost the Vienna stock exchange. He sees big potential for privatisations by Austria's provinces.
- Beverage group BBAG's chief executive Johannes Brandl plans to restructure the company with a possible merger of its subsidiary breweries Brau AG and Steirerbrau.
- Austria's border police discovered a record number of 95 Kurds trying to enter the country illegally in the back of a truck.
- Austria celebrates Renate Goetschl as the country's first women's downhill skiing world cup winner in 18 years.
DIE PRESSE
- Belgian savings bank Bacob is a likely partner for Die Erste savings bank to finance the latter's takeover of GiroCredit.
- The Raiffeisen banking group is no longer interested in buying a stake in Bank Austria.

- German insurer Allianz's Austrian units are looking for a bank to become a sales partner. The Austrian groups' 1996 pre-tax profits fell slightly in 1996 to 558.4 million schillings from 561.6 million schillings. The dividend is to remain unchanged.
KURIER

- While constructor Ferro-Betonit has just been taken over by Alpine Bau, Bank Austria's stake in Stuag is to be sold next, in order to comply with the European Commission's ruling for Bank Austria's takeover of Creditanstalt.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN

- The state's stake in PSK is the next privatisation planned. Austrian banks GiroCredit, Raiffeisen and Bawag are interested. Bank Austria will present on Monday its future strategy following its takeover of Creditanstalt.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Bank Austria plans to present its swap offers for Creditanstalt share holders as soon as possible.
